claim: TRIZ founding numbers (patent counts, five levels of inventiveness, how the matrix was derived) could not be verified from any opened source; the method is a patent-derived catalogue of reframes, not a tested theory of thought.
agent_test: Treat TRIZ claims as design heuristics; require each reframe operator to pay for itself at equal tokens.

claim: Human ideation: TRIZ-taught first-year teams produced about twice as many feasible concepts (8.94 vs 4.42 per team) in an unrandomised classroom comparison under instructor supervision (re-checked in the paper text).
agent_test: Quantity-only evidence; run matched-token typed reframe vs free reframe and count distinct feasible answers.

claim: A controlled multi-site replication did not reproduce the quantity gain: TRIZ raised novelty and variety and slightly lowered quantity (quantity p 0.29-0.63; novelty p 0.0004 to 0.58 across sites). Gap search: the 2013 journal paper reports the same UTEP/UMD experiment as the 2012 paper, so these are one experiment family from one lab group, not two replications.
agent_test: Measure on the agent: a typed reframe should raise answer-set variety at some cost in count; compare diversity at equal tokens.

claim: Structured TRIZ sessions shift design effort to problem aspects (goals, requirements) rather than solutions (index 0.526 vs 0.192, p=0.001); the gap shrinks by the second half.
agent_test: Check whether the typed reframe works only by forcing problem restatement: compare with a plain 'restate the problem first' step at equal tokens.

claim: Matrix and principle methods beat a no-method control in a 72-pair student study (MaTriz 2.3/3.1/3.5 vs control 0.7/1.1/1.6) but the edge over SCAMPER is small and the control came from one university.
agent_test: Compare typed principle lists against a plain SCAMPER-style checklist and a no-method arm.

claim: LLMs detect that a TRIZ contradiction exists far better than they recover the right improving/worsening pair (detection F1 0.75-0.90 vs pair F1 0.29-0.45; patent pair Hit@3 0.13-0.28).
agent_test: Score the agent's stated trade-off pair against a gold set; gate reframe use on a code check that both sides are present and cited.

claim: LLM contradiction finders over-fire: GPT-4 flagged contradictions in 86 of 100 patents annotated contradiction-free; on annotated patents precision was 0.46 (re-checked in the paper). Label error cannot be ruled out.
agent_test: A trade-off trigger must be gated on a failing check, not on the model saying it sees a trade-off; measure the false-trigger rate on neutral items.

claim: For picking inventive principles, matrix lookup plus an LLM reranker beats direct LLM prompting (Hit@3 0.71/0.59 vs 0.39-0.52 / 0.25-0.35). Correction: the matrix baseline is given the gold improve/worsen pair; the end-to-end version with predicted pairs scores lower (0.59/0.46 zero-shot) but still above direct prompting.
agent_test: Code produces the candidate set from a table; the model only selects. Test against free 'name a principle' at equal tokens, with a random top-3 baseline (about 7.5 percent for one gold principle).

claim: Direct LLM principle prompting is plausible but weakly anchored; label accuracy can be right while cited evidence is wrong, and the reverse.
agent_test: Require each reframe to cite source spans and check in code that the span exists.

claim: Few-shot exemplars narrowed TRIZ output and cut contradiction recall by about 45 points (0.69 to 0.25) in GPT-4; chain-of-thought gave the best recall; solution-writing quality did not differ by prompt strategy (cosine 0.823-0.829, n.s.).
agent_test: Let code decide how many candidate reframes to carry; ask for several and filter. Test exemplar vs no-exemplar reframe count.

claim: Contradiction choice by GPT-4 is unstable across 100 samples (entropy up to 6.64 bits; 7 of 10 textbook cases matched or half-matched within top 3); higher-frequency detections matched the textbook better. The authors chose not to majority-vote, since different valid contradictions give different valid solutions.
agent_test: Count samples in code; use frequency to order trials, not as proof. Same-model samples are not independent.

claim: Model strength helps only under some prompts: GPT-4 beat GPT-3.5 on 10 post-cutoff cases with basic and CoT prompts (0.544 vs 0.400) but not with few-shot; GPT-3.5 dropped parameter numbers in 2 of 10 outputs.
agent_test: Validate reframe output schema in code; test each scaffold element against the plain model.

claim: Retrieval of TRIZ definitions plus reranking plus a structured prompt raised parameter-extraction F1 from 76.9 to 84.2 on one dataset, but the preprint shows signs of pasted text and gives no model names.
agent_test: Low priority; do not rely on the numbers. Own test: glossary vs no glossary at equal tokens.

claim: In a text-to-CAD case a vanilla 'make it lighter' prompt cut more mass (-31.8%) but raised stress 64.1% and deflection 99.4%; only 1 of 4 TRIZ principles kept stress flat (Segmentation -14.7% mass, -0.1% stress). One chair, one run each (re-checked in the paper table). Gap search: re-read; per-principle rows are #1 -14.7%/-0.1%/+0.7%, #8 -5.9%/+21.6%/+4.4%, #15 -4.0%/+33.2%/+16.3%, #40 -10.0%/+40.7%/+44.4% (mass/stress/displacement). N=1 per cell, not token-matched.
agent_test: A typed principle changes the kind of answer; verify with an outcome check and repeat runs for variance.

claim: An agent-loop use of TRIZ operators with gates improved F1 by +0.15 to +4.23 points on three datasets, but the authors state the gains cannot be assigned to TRIZ versus search or scoring; the 45-activity campaign failed its own frozen gate (+1.90% vs 3.2277% required). Gap search: the authors state no equal-budget unguided control was run, so the gain cannot be credited to TRIZ.
agent_test: Matched-budget ablation: typed TRIZ operator vs untyped mutation vs random mutation, with declare-before-result and a promotion gate.

claim: No published study compares a TRIZ-structured prompt with a matched-token plain prompt using blind-rated novelty or correctness; LLM+TRIZ evidence is case studies and benchmarks (1 to 47 cases) plus one 1,354-case benchmark.
agent_test: This is the central test to run in our harness.

claim: AutoTRIZ's central claim (LLM+TRIZ beats LLM alone) is untested in the paper; its battery-cooling gains (206 vs 166 Wh/L, 21.66 vs 13.18 eTMS, 43% vs 34% grouping; re-checked) come from one case with expert-selected ideas and no baseline.
agent_test: Do not cite as evidence of effect.

claim: Multi-agent role-played TRIZ is expensive and partly missed targets: 150,000-250,000 tokens per run on one case, one of two case solutions found, the TRIZ specialist skipped its retrieval tool.
agent_test: Compare against a single call at equal tokens; make lookups compulsory in code.

claim: Cross-method agreement from one small model (IdeaForge, TinyLlama 1.1B) is not independent evidence; the top score came from counting convergent links.
agent_test: Do not count agreement across prompts from one model as confirmation.

claim: Ideal final result as a stand-alone prompt step has no measured LLM effect; it appears only as an Ideality score in TRIZ-a and as a prompt step inside pipelines.
agent_test: Test 'ideal result: the function happens with no new part' as a typed reframe vs a plain 'simplify' prompt at equal tokens.

claim: Running all 40 principles blindly with GPT-3.5 gives many ideas but many do not resolve the contradiction; functional-analysis accuracy was about 50%.
agent_test: Filter principles by matrix first, then score by code.

claim: Human users find the matrix lookup tedious and drift from the chosen principle without supervision; LLM help lowers workload but did not always improve quality on complex tasks.
agent_test: Move lookup into code; add a code monitor for drift from the chosen principle.

claim: A 'more novel, fewer ideas' trade appears across stimulus-based ideation methods (patent analogies in 153 seniors; TRIZ), not only TRIZ.
agent_test: Measure whether a typed reframe lowers answer count while raising spread.

claim: TRIZBench reports no random or prior-frequency baseline. Uniform chance for Hit@3 is 7.5% (1 gold principle), 14.6% (2), 21.4% (3), 27.7% (4). All reported Hit@3 values (0.25-0.71) sit above uniform chance, but the fair floor, a principle-frequency prior, was never run.
agent_test: Compute a frequency-prior top-3 baseline on any principle-selection test before crediting the selector.

claim: End-to-end principle selection (model predicts the pair, then matrix lookup) is 10-12 Hit@3 points below the gold-pair version for Qwen3-8B (0.59 vs 0.71 on cases, 0.46 vs 0.59 on patents) and does not beat TF-IDF retrieval (0.69, 0.56). The gold-pair figures overstate what a pipeline gets.
agent_test: Verify the improve/worsen slots with a code check before the lookup; report end-to-end numbers only.

claim: TRIZ gain in novelty is larger for people with stronger relational reasoning (abstract-level finding, no sample size or coefficient obtained).
agent_test: Test the typed reframe on weak and strong models; expect weaker analogy ability to gain less.

claim: Less abstract wording of the principles gives more ideas in a 10-minute student exercise (three groups, three problems; abstract only).
agent_test: Store each principle with a one-line concrete example in the code-held table; test with and without.

claim: Second-hand report: randomly chosen design heuristics improved human design outcomes. If principle choice matters little, forced restatement may carry the effect. Primary papers not opened.
agent_test: Include a random-principle arm and a restate-only arm in the first matched-token test.

claim: Recent Springer IFIP TRIZ-with-LLM chapters (ARIZ, contradiction processing, cognitive skills) could not be opened; no controlled numbers are known from them. Gaps 1, 2, 5, 7, 8 and 9 remain unmeasured in every source reachable.
agent_test: Plan the matched-token experiment ourselves; the literature will not supply it.
